text:
Marta: Quick sync -- after the RFC I wanted to surface a few follow-ups about the console query path and RBAC pushdown tradeoffs.
Josh: yup, curious what you found.
Marta: tl;dr: pushing auth checks deeper (edge) buys us latency but complicates batching and cache invalidation.
Devin: can you sketch a concrete example?
Marta: imagine dashboard tile A and B share a prefetched prefix. If we evaluate RBAC at edge per-tenant, we can return cached KV faster. But when permissions change, cache keys need tenant-scoped invalidation which spikes churn.
Josh: so edge pushdown = lower p95 but higher cache invalidation rate and storage blowup.
Liam: and more metadata per cache entry -> memory overhead.
Devin: what about hybrid? do global cache + per-response filter at control plane?
Marta: that's the hybrid we prototyped. Control plane stores canonical results, edge applies a small permission delta filter. Pros: fewer invalidations. Cons: filter step adds ~2-4ms depending on predicate complexity.
Josh: 2-4ms is okay for bulk of dashboards, but some panels are latency-sensitive (stream previews).
Liam: also hybrid means more CPU at edge for filters, so cost shifts from cache storage to compute.
Marta: right. Another idea: encode a permissive bitmap in cache key for common permission tiers to avoid per-tenant keys.
Devin: that sounds promising but increases key cardinality combinatorially if we support many roles.
Josh: can we limit to 3 tiers (owner/editor/viewer) and fall back to control-plane filter for custom perms?
Marta: yes, that reduces cardinality a lot in practice. Usage histogram shows 80% fall into those tiers.
Liam: action: quantify cache hit improvement vs memory growth for 3-tier vs tenant-keyed. I can run cluster sim later today.
sre-bot: deploy-check: remember the feature flag gating for any auth path change.
Marta: good call. We definitely need canary + opt-out. Josh, thoughts on rollout?
Josh: start with canary on non-critical orgs, enable telemetry for hit rates, invalidations, and end-to-end p95. If any signal regresses, auto-roll back.
Devin: one more perf nuance: batching. Our continuous-batching runtime assumes identical auth scope to coalesce. If we pushdown auth to edge, requests diverge and batching efficiency drops.
Marta: exact. We measured 30% fewer coalesced batches when auth is tenant-scoped.
Josh: Could we batch at prefix-level before auth expands the scope? E.g., batch on identical model+prompt prefix, then post-process per-tenant.
Devin: that's feasible if post-processing is cheap. For heavy post-filtering we'd lose the benefit.
Liam: another operational trade: debugging incidents. If auth logic lives at edge, stack traces span more services and we need correlated traces plus permission-policy snapshots.
Marta: ops burden increases. We'll need to log policy revision IDs with responses.
Josh: logging idea: add header X-Auth-Proto: v2-{policy_id} so we can correlate. Keep header small.
Marta: agreed. Also suggest a new telemetry event: auth_invalidation.{tenant,policy} to understand churn.
Devin: about the UI side: we might add a graceful degrade UI for panels that miss SLO due to filter step. Small skeleton with "partial data" instead of full error.
Liam: UX ok with that?
Josh: product likes partials for availability. Need copy.
Marta: implementation sketch (config):
```
auth.path: edge|hybrid|control
cache.key.scheme: tenant|tiered|global
batching.scope: strict|prefix-then-filter
feature_flag.console_auth_refactor: off
```
Marta: rollout plan: 1) run simulation for memory/hit tradeoffs (Liam), 2) implement tiered cache prototype + telemetry (Devin + Marta), 3) canary hybrid mode (Josh ops), 4) measure and iterate.
Liam: I'll post sim results by EOD. Expecting ~2x cache size for tenant-keyed, ~1.15x for 3-tier.
Devin: I'll wire telemetry hooks and add the header.
Josh: I'll prepare canary playbook and rollback knobs.
sre-bot: reminder: include performance budget in the canary (p50/p95/p99 and batch-coalescing rate).
Marta: final question for the thread: are we comfortable accepting a 3ms median penalty for hybrid in exchange for much lower invalidation churn and simpler ops?
Josh: yes for most dashboards. For stream previews we should keep control-plane quickpath.
Devin: agree. We'll pattern-match per-route.
Liam: +1. I'll add route-exception list to the config.
Marta: cool — thanks everyone. I'll write a short RFC follow-up with decisions and the experiment checklist.
Josh: thanks, nice tradeoff breakdown.
Devin: thanks.
Liam: thanks, ping when sims done.
Marta: closing thread, will file the follow-up RFC.
